summary.intent: Audit whether the checker-request bug pattern (sending fields tsrs ignores) exists elsewhere, decide on semantic changes, establish a merge order with change/PR numbers, and update the related PRs accordingly.
summary.outcome: Audit found the pattern isn't elsewhere in the checked request shapes; a trial merge showed only #506 vs #509 conflict in `composes`; merge order was set (diagnostics fix, #506, #508, #509). The CONTRIBUTING.md update for #505 (three lessons) was linted and committed locally; the diagnostics fix push and #506/#509 notes were not yet done, and two background audits were still running.

repo: tsrs_api has a paramfields.rs table of accepted parameter names per method; unknown keys are silently ignored (like Go), so a wrong field name in a checker request fails silently. This allows a mechanical audit of requests sent vs accepted.
Six checker methods have no paramfields table entry; their handlers had to be inspected directly to see which keys they read.
Pre-push bar is `just lint doc-check machete typos`, plus workspace tests (1,702 passing) and a checker lane.

With collapse off, spectrum's private-field names (e.g. `__#8@#type`) embed a checker id that varies with the number of requests; stripping it first would make #509 byte-identical across configurations.
Trail 405 maps PRs to changes: #505=caliper/303, #506=caliper/304, #507=caliper/305, #508=caliper/306, #509=caliper/307; #497 is the unrelated 0.11.0 release PR.
The #509 single-flight cache is a reusable primitive for future scheduling and session-reuse work.

code.finding: `composes` is the conflict site between #506 (`below_react` flag) and #509 (cached `alias_arguments`); resolution is to keep both. Exact line numbers were not given in the transcript.

workflow: Trial-merge all pending PR branches onto a scratch branch, then abort and delete it, to find conflicts and decide merge order without changing anything.
Add a regression test asserting each request's parameters change the checker's answer, since unknown fields are ignored.
Benchmarks should reject runs with checker fallback and combine measured combinations rather than summing independent estimates.
Parallel read-and-measure sub-agents can run audits while the main thread writes up findings.
